notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41808049/cb05e6f014744ce0f850c8425d5a4128b36a9422.gif[/img]

[h1]Matchpoint Update 1.8[/h1]

[i]Tennis fans watch out![/i]

[b]Matchpoint - Tennis Championships – Update 1.8[/b] has just been [b]released for Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 4|5[/b].
The update includes a fix for Tiebreakers that could start with an incorrect score. 
In addition, Update 1.8 fixes the multiplayer achievement “Schooled” not unlocking after 25 wins on Xbox.

[b]More details can be found in the full changelog below[/b]

[i]Game on!
Your Matchpoint – Tennis Championships Team[/i]

[h2]Changelog:[/h2]
[list][*] Fixed an issue where Tiebreakers would begin with an incorrect score.
[*] Fixed an issue where a second controller would not connect to local multiplayer in certain circumstances.
[*] Fixed an issue where the aim marker could remain off after playing ranked multiplayer.
[*] Improved lobby connection.
[*] Updated the game intro to the latest version.
[*] [Xbox consoles] Fixed “Schooled” achievement not unlocking when winning 25 online matches.
[*] [PlayStation consoles] Fixed issue where an online ID would not update in the Block List if the user changed their name. [/list]

notes.title: Matchpoint – Tennis Championships - Update 1.7
notes.content:
[h1]Matchpoint – Tennis Championships - Update 1.7[/h1]

[i]Tennis fans watch out![/i]

[b]Matchpoint - Tennis Championships – Update 1.7 has just been released for Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 4|5.[/b]

There are fixes for the multiplayer and adjustments to the ELO system in Matchpoint – Tennis Championships 1.7, as well as for an issue that led to, the aim marker lags in multiplayer mode and an issue with the match score that led to neverending matches.

The update also includes fixes for the freezes and crashes on PlayStation 4 and fixes the issues for some players on Gamepass (PC) that previously were not able to connect to multiplayer or invite other players.

Thank you for your feedback and your suggestions, we are happy to receive your thoughts and will continue to work on improvements for the game.

More details can be found in the full changelog:

[i]Game on![/i]

[list][*] [PS4] Fixed an issue that could lead to freezes and occasional crashes. 
[*] [Multiplayer] [Game Pass PC] Fixed authentication issues for some players that previously were not able to connect to multiplayer or invite other players.
[*] [Xbox] Fixed an error that led to the 'You did it' achievement not being triggered
[*] Added variable delay to the A.I. serve time, to give the user time to adjust positions
[*] Improved memory management by cleaning up scenes correctly, which also fixes some crashes
[*] Optimizations regarding an issue with controller dis- and re-connection.
[*] Camera updates and improvements
[*] Fixed scoring related issues that were being caused by saving/loading career matches
[*] Fixed a camera issue that was occurring on one of the stadiums
[*] Fixed incorrect location images displaying for some tournaments.
[*] Fixed a clipping issue in Training court
[*] Fixed an UI issue where buttons were no longer highlighted when cancelling confirmation popups
[*] Fixed an issue where the user could activate career options while exiting career mode
[*] Fixed issue where player would walk against invisible wall during serve animation
[*] Fixed an issue where the crowd didn't appear under certain circumstances
[*] Fixed a display issue with the Chinese flag
[*] Improvements to the UI popup system, which also fixes some bugs
[*] Fixed an issue with incorrect scores that could also lead to an endless match.
[*] Fixed incorrect call outs from the commentator regarding strengths/weaknesses and set point/match point.
[*] Fixed the sorting of the ranked trophies.
[*] Localization improvements
[*] [Multiplayer] Fixed region not being saved correctly when joining a game via an invite code.
[*] [Multiplayer] Fixed a bug that prevented showing the post-match flow in multiplayer after leaving through the pause menu
[*] [Multiplayer] Fixed an issue that resulted in the aim marker lagging in multiplayer matches.
[*] [Multiplayer] Aim marker is now turned off in Ranked Multiplayer and the option is removed in the settings menu
[*] [Multiplayer] Fixed some bugs related to the timeout for idling in Multiplayer. Also, the inactivity timer on "Invite a friend" has been removed.[/list]

[b]Several changes to the ELO System[/b]
[list][*] Fixed some bugs that resulted in ELO calculation errors
[*] Adjusted the ELO ranges being searched for when playing ranked matches. The longer you search for a match, the bigger the ELO range that is being searched for. Qualifying matches have a bigger impact on your ELO now
[*] Fixed a bug that showed ELO changes during qualification matches.
[*] Fixed an issue where the ELO was calculated incorrectly after leaving a match.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Master Rank trophy wouldn't display after reaching or exceeding 2200 ELO.
[*] Fixed the display and overlapping of 4 digit ELO points.[/list]

notes.title: New Dev Diary! Go Racket to Racket with Cross-Platform Multiplayer
notes.content:
[h1]Go Racket to Racket with Cross-Platform Multiplayer in Matchpoint – Tennis Championships[/h1]

We are happy to confirm that Matchpoint – Tennis Championships will feature [b]cross-platform multiplayer[/b], so you can put your tennis skills to the test [b]across all announced platforms[/b]. You can truly put your tennis skills to the test as you rally with friends and challenge competitors across multiple platforms. Delve deeper into the brand-new title in the latest Developer Diary video which explores multiplayer mode and the game’s other thrilling features.

[b]Join Producer Kevin McIntosh and Game Designer Dave McIntosh[/b] as they discuss all things Matchpoint and delve into some of the features that you will experience in your journey to becoming World #1. From choosing the right coach to implementing the best play style, this second Developer Diary video provides insight into the game’s true-to-life tennis tactics that will put your skills and decision-making to the test. Whether its career management or going racket to racket in the game’s newly announced [b]cross-platform multiplayer mode[/b], Matchpoint – Tennis Championships is packed with exciting and dynamic features that combine to create an authentic tennis gameplay experience.

Matchpoint – Tennis Championships will be released with [b]Xbox Game Pass for console and PC and will be available on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S consoles (supported through Smart Delivery), PlayStation 4|5 and Windows PC on 7th July 2022[/b]. The title will be available on [b]Nintendo Switch™ on 20th October 2022[/b]. Spinning with excitement? The tennis simulator game is now available for pre-order with a 10% discount on the Kalypso, Microsoft and Sony stores!

[h3]Check out the newest Developer Diary below:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=Obj3w0YD-cQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list][*] [b]Enter the world of professional Tennis.[/b] Matchpoint – Tennis Championships offers a deep career mode featuring a unique merit-based ranking system.
[*] [b]Create your own 3D tennis star.[/b] Choose your look, fashion and play style with an array of customization options including true to life techniques such as left-or right-handed, onehanded or twohanded backhand.
[*] [b]Dominate the court as a tennis professional.[/b] Matchpoint - Tennis Championships features 16 real-life international tennis stars from the professional circuit, like Nick Kyrgios, Kei Nishikori or Amanda Anisimova, including their gear from brands such as Nike, Yonex, Babolat and many more! 
[*] [b]Customize your athlete and wearables.[/b] From rackets to clothing, create your own tennis star and unlock special equipment by winning competitive matches.
[*] [b]Master all strokes and shots in grand style.[/b] Determine the outcome of a rally by choosing the best technique for the time: top spin, flat, lob or slice shot.
[*] [b]Take on opponents in local or online matches.[/b] Play against a cunning AI or face your friends and rivals on the court via local sessions and online cross-play.
[*] [b]Study your rival’s moves and tactics.[/b] Watch your opponents and get to know their strengths and weaknesses to gain a tactical advantage before you even hit the court.
[*] [b]Practice makes perfect:[/b] hire a personal coach to hone your skills. Buff your strengths and diminish your weaknesses with an in-game coaching system of individual training modules.
[*] [b]Fine-tune your tactics in Practice and Mini-Game modes:[/b] Jump into a variety of mini-games to hone your perfect game and become a force to be reckoned with on the court.
[*] [b]Compete in exhibition matches at spectacular venues around the globe.[/b] Each court has its own characteristics; study your arenas of play and adapt your game to grass, clay and hard courts.
[*] [b]Replay mode.[/b] Breakpoint or deciding match point, capture your fiercest rallies on film and study the outcomes to improve your game.
[/list]

notes.title: Matchpoint – Tennis Championships: Demo Update
notes.content:
[h1]Matchpoint – Tennis Championships: Demo Update [/h1]

As Matchpoint – Tennis Championships is gearing up for its launch on [b]July 7th[/b], we’ve just [b]updated the demo available on Steam[/b]. Along with this update, we also made the [b]demo available for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 with the Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S version following shortly. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41808049/cb05e6f014744ce0f850c8425d5a4128b36a9422.gif[/img]

The Steam demo update includes the following [b]changes[/b]:
[list][*] Added ball trail toggle to the settings menu 
[*] A.I. error chance has been significantly reduced 
[*] Updates to the animation system to better handle volleys (they no longer play out of time) and running back shots 
[*] Racket roll improved, so we don't see the racket spinning when it shouldn't be 
[*] Fixed some input issues on PC when disconnecting a controller 
[*] Fixed bug where opponents would vanish during transitions 
[*] Fixed bug where replay couldn't be played on second point of each game in quick match 
[*] Fixed bug where sometimes the ball wouldn't line up with the racket 
[*] Updates for clothing, licensors and brands 
[*] Fix to an issue where the player's position/speed could abruptly change coming out of a shot animation 
[*] Fixed an issue where the ball would appear late out of the hand while serving 
[*] Fixed bug where the commentator VO would fade out when pausing/unpausing 
[*] Fixed female legs clipping through shorts with low graphics settings [/list]

notes.title: MATCHPOINT - TENNIS CHAMPIONSHIPS
notes.content:
[h1]Prepare for game, set,
MATCHPOINT - TENNIS CHAMPIONSHIPS [/h1]
[h2]Kalypso announces new sports franchise with authentic tennis simulator[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41808049/87524b945d8fe76a2c9089c90985dd2bb12dba06.png[/img]

[h3]Information[/h3]
[b]Title:[/b] Matchpoint - Tennis Championships
[b]Platforms:[/b] Windows PC, Xbox (One, Series X|S), PlayStation 4|5, Nintendo Switch™
[b]Developer:[/b] Torus Games
[b]Genre:[/b] Tennis Simulator
[b]Release:[/b] Spring 2022
[b]Hashtag:[/b] #MatchpointGame


Kalypso Media and Australian developer Torus Games have today announced Matchpoint - Tennis Championships, a brand-new title that delivers authentic gameplay and an immersive tennis experience. Matchpoint - Tennis Championships is scheduled for release in Spring 2022 for PlayStation 4|5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch™.

An immersive announcement trailer gives a first look into the tennis simulator, which focuses on realistic scenarios and player reactions in the exciting world of tennis. By using the right tactics, intelligent player positioning, and utilizing authentic ball physics which are a central part of the gameplay – players will be able to top the tennis tables in tournaments and competitions around the world. Sophisticated character animations and unprecedented player control are combined within Matchpoint – Tennis Championships, creating realistic rallies in which every swing of the racket counts.

[previewyoutube=uHnIP7OCtH4;full][/previewyoutube]

As a modern tennis game, Matchpoint - Tennis Championships promises a dynamic and immersive gaming experience with an extensive career mode and a unique rivalry system. At the time of release, 16 well-known tennis stars will be integrated into Matchpoint - Tennis Championships. From the current number two in the world ranking list Danill Medvedev – to other top ten world ranked players such as Garbiñe Muguruza, Andrey Rublev, Casper Ruud and Hubert Hurkaczs. More renowned players will also be playable, with Nick Kyrgios, Benoît Paire, Heather Watson, Hugo Gaston, Madison Keys, Victoria Azarenka, Carlos Alcaraz, and Pablo Carreno Busta.

Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova, and Kei Nishikori will also be part of the launch, and together with Garbine Muguruza and Danill Medvedev – they have expressed their enthusiasm and anticipation for Matchpoint - Tennis Championships in the included video testimonials.

[previewyoutube=aEi-4FUkIfk;full][/previewyoutube]

The integration of sports and fashion brands such as Uniqlo, Nike, and Head, all integrated into the game and the players' equipment, will also add an authentic atmosphere in Matchpoint - Tennis Championships.
 
[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Enter the world of professional Tennis: “Matchpoint - Tennis Championships” offers a deep career mode featuring a unique merit-based ranking system.
[*] Create your 3D tennis star. Choose your look, fashion, and play style with an array of customization options, including true-to-life techniques such as left-or right-handed, one-handed, or two-handed backhand.
[*] [b]Dominate the court as a tennis professional.[/b] Matchpoint - Tennis Championships features 16 real-life international tennis stars from the professional circuit, like Nick Kyrgios, Kei Nishikori or Amanda Anisimova, including their gear from brands such as Nike, Yonex, Babolat and many more! 
[*] [b]Customize your athlete and wearables.[/b] From rackets to clothing, create your own tennis star and unlock special equipment by winning competitive matches.
[*] Master all strokes and shots in grand style. Determine the outcome of a rally by choosing the best technique for the time: topspin, flat, lob or slice shot.
[*] Take on opponents in local or online matches: Defeat challenging AI opponents or challenge your friends and rivals to a virtual tennis duel.
[*] Study your rival’s moves and tactics. Watch your opponents and get to know their strengths and weaknesses to gain a tactical advantage before you even hit the court.
[*] Practice makes perfect: Hire a personal coach to hone your skills. Enhance your strengths and diminish your weaknesses with an in-game coaching system of individual training modules.
[*] Fine-tune your tactics in Practice and Training modes: Jump into various mini-games to hone your perfect game and become a force to be reckoned with on the court.
[*] Compete in exhibition matches at spectacular venues around the globe. Each court has its unique characteristics; study your arenas of play and adapt your game to grass, clay, and hard courts.
[*] Replay mode. Capture your fiercest rallies and decisive matchpoints on film and study the outcomes to improve your game.
[/list]
